title: Coherent power semilinearity and normalized etale power comparison
statement: Let X be proper over a field k and let FrZ be an additive endomorphism of the underlying Zariski structure sheaf that is sectionwise pth power. In every degree q, coherent Frobenius [def-pbc-canonical-coherent-etale-comparison] is p-semilinear for the scalarCohomology k-action. Moreover, for every additive endomorphism FrE of the lifted tensor-section etale structure sheaf that is sectionwise pth power under tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit, the normalized coherent-to-etale comparison intertwines FrZ and FrE. The semilinearity assertion does not require supplying an etale endomorphism. The two power maps are assumed additive, so the statement needs no additional prime or characteristic hypotheses.

proof.text: Use a finite affine cover of X and separated affine tuple intersections. Affine module vanishing, restriction of injectives, module/abelian comparison, and etale object vanishing give tuple acyclicity on both sites.

Identify the section complexes by the normalized unit pullback. The site-change Cech edge square gives a family on all quasi-coherent modules that is natural, normalized in degree zero and compatible with connecting maps. The uniqueness in the definition identifies it with normalizedCoherentEtaleComparison. The module/abelian edge is the fixed resolution comparison by its normalization on injective resolutions.

On every tuple the supplied two endomorphisms are the same power map. Additive coefficient naturality of the acyclic edges proves the square on Cech classes. Their surjectivity gives the assertion for all cohomology classes, including q=0 and the empty scheme.

Multiplication by a scalar is a module coefficient morphism, acts termwise on a resolution and hence acts by the scalar on module cohomology. Thus the module Cech edge is scalar-linear. On the common section complex, Fr(a*z)=a^p*Fr(z); transport through the fixed comparison and the Cech edge to obtain coherent semilinearity. This argument requires no etale endomorphism, so the scalar result precedes the universally quantified etale map.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentPowerComparison
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (p q : ℕ)
    (FrZ : (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).obj (unit X) ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).obj (unit X))
    (hFrZ : ∀ (U : X.Opensᵒᵖ) (s : Γ(X, U.unop)), FrZ.hom.app U s = s ^ p) :
    (∀ (a : k) (v : scalarCohomology f (unit X) q),
      structureCoherentFrobenius f q FrZ (a • v) =
        a ^ p • structureCoherentFrobenius f q FrZ v) ∧
    ∀ (FrE : structureTensorEtaleSheaf X ⟶ structureTensorEtaleSheaf X)
    (hFrE : ∀ (U : X.Etaleᵒᵖ) (s : (structureTensorEtaleSheaf X).obj.obj U),
      (tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit U.unop.hom).app ⊤ (FrE.hom.app U s).down =
        (@id Γ(U.unop.left, ⊤)
          ((tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit U.unop.hom).app ⊤ s.down)) ^ p)
    (x : @Sheaf.H _ _ (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).obj (unit X))
      inferInstance (HasExt.standard _) q),
    normalizedCoherentEtaleComparison f (unit X) q
        (@Sheaf.H.map _ _ _ inferInstance (HasExt.standard _) _ _ FrZ q x) =
      Sheaf.H.map FrE q (normalizedCoherentEtaleComparison f (unit X) q x)
